quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?

options.text: Slow down at the light.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. You must yield to all traffic and pedestrians before proceeding. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices turn off before going.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass only if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive so slowly that you block normal traffic movement, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky behavior.
Nothing to be concerned about.
No less safe than driving under any other conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It endangers you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers. Staying focused on driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're trying to pass.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Rush ahead to pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give plenty of space. Bicyclists have little protection. Passing too quickly can force them off course.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A dashed white line can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if you are involved in an accident?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle immediately. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help with severe bleeding using direct pressure. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead winds with a series of turns or curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet and is harder to drive on safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
Upcoming hill.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming hill.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead. Adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show sharp road curves in the direction of the arrow. This sign indicates a sharp left curve. Several chevron signs may appear throughout the curve.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning so other drivers know your plan. Slow down and stay in the right lane, as close as you can to the right curb or road edge.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop. Stay stopped as long as the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is out.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, then turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: If you cannot see clearly at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.
questions.explanation: Always slow down at intersections. If you cannot see traffic clearly, stop completely. Then inch forward carefully until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.question: Under ideal driving conditions, what following distance rule should you use?

options.text: Two-second
One-second
Half-second
Half-mile

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-second
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between your car and the vehicle ahead in good conditions. In wet or icy conditions, increase this to three or four seconds. Always increase your distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: The road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line in the center. If the broken line is next to your lane, what does it mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass. A solid line on the other side means oncoming traffic cannot pass. Only pass if no vehicles are coming toward you.

questions.question: When exiting an expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up on the exit ramp.
Check the speed limit sign for the road you are entering.
Cut across other traffic.
Do not use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the speed limit sign for the road you are entering.
questions.explanation: Watch traffic carefully when exiting. Look at the new speed limit sign and check your speedometer. The new road will likely have a lower speed limit than the expressway.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware. Do not stare straight ahead only. In fog, use low beam lights, not high beams.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Press yourself against the seat and head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.
